overview: The Council approved a common victualler license for Medford Brewing Company and advanced a preliminary funding plan for citywide water meter replacements. Councilors also took up numerous resolutions on transit, DCR infrastructure, housing, and city finances, sending several matters to committees for further review.

items.title: Approval of Minutes and Committee Reports
items.summary: The Council tabled the July 19 minutes until later in the meeting and approved a Committee of the Whole report concerning the MBTA bus redesign project.

items.title: Condolences, Congratulations, and Recognitions
items.summary: The Council passed resolutions offering condolences on the passing of retired employee Jerry Perlito, congratulating Donald and Mary Bonner on their 50th wedding anniversary, and recognizing City Solicitor Kimberly Scanlon for over 20 years of service upon her departure.

items.title: Public Participation on Medford Square Parking
items.summary: Chamber of Commerce representatives urged the city to explore a public-private partnership to construct a parking garage in Medford Square, prompting council discussion on past funding, zoning changes, and potential multi-use structures.

items.title: Common Victualler License for Medford Brewing Company
items.summary: Approved a common victualler license for Nicholas Belytheau and Max Heinegg to operate Medford Brewing Company at 30 Harvard Avenue.

items.title: CPA Grants for Elementary School Playgrounds
items.summary: Approved $10,000 from the CPA General Reserve ($5,000 each) to replace playground elements at Roberts Elementary School and Brooks Elementary School.

items.title: Water Meter Replacement Project Funding
items.summary: Approved a motion authorizing the mayor to initiate the application process for a $7.8 million, 10-year interest-free MWRA loan to fund an $8.5 million citywide water meter replacement project, alongside $700,000 in ARPA funds.

items.title: Law Department Settlement
items.summary: Approved a $5,000 settlement payment for a claim by Claire Rooney arising from a street defect on Harvard Avenue.

items.title: Restaurant Bar Seating Formula
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting that the Liquor Commission review and consider increasing the maximum limit of 25 bar seats for Medford restaurants.

items.title: Parking Kiosk Issues
items.summary: Referred a resolution to the Committee of the Whole regarding non-functioning parking kiosks that fail to take cash or credit cards and broader parking department operations.

items.title: Revenue Planning and Budget Shortfall
items.summary: Following discussion on ballot deadlines and city finances, the Council voted 4-3 to amend an unviable November override ballot paper into a general request for a Committee of the Whole meeting with the mayor and finance staff regarding structural revenue shortfalls.

items.title: Private Way Rules and Maintenance
items.summary: Referred a resolution to the Rules and Ordinances subcommittee to clarify city services and regulations for private ways under Chapter 74 of the city ordinances.

items.title: DCR Fellsway Sidewalks and State Agency Coordination
items.summary: Approved a merged and amended resolution calling for meetings with the state legislative delegation regarding DCR oversight, requesting a report from the DPW commissioner on the Fellsway asphalt sidewalk replacements within 10 days, and advocating to preserve concrete sidewalks.

items.title: Road Maintenance and Crack Sealing
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting an update from the administration on crack sealing practices and road maintenance funding in light of the city's pavement management backlog.

items.title: Bradley Road Tenant Displacement
items.summary: Received and placed on file an update from the Bradley Road Tenants Association detailing mass no-fault eviction notices, lack of negotiations, and court summonses affecting residents.

items.title: Reproductive Rights Protections
items.summary: Referred a resolution to the Public Health and Community Safety subcommittee to consider municipal policies protecting reproductive health access, with an amendment to invite local healthcare representatives.

items.title: East Albion Street Connection
items.summary: Approved a resolution asking the administration to investigate opening the blocked-off border connection on East Albion Street to pedestrian and bicycle access between Medford and Somerville.

items.title: Bipartisan Infrastructure Law Grant Applications
items.summary: Approved a resolution asking the administration for updates on federal infrastructure applications, specifically the Safe Streets for All program and the Reconnecting Communities pilot.

items.title: National Grid Power Outages
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting National Grid provide information on recurrent neighborhood outages and outline local grid modernization plans.

items.title: Playing Field Striping Equipment
items.summary: Approved an inquiry asking the administration about the cost, acquisition, and lifespan of newly acquired athletic field striping machines.

items.title: Orange Line Shutdown and MBTA Bus Routes
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting the MBTA reinstate discontinued bus routes, ensure adequate shuttles during the Orange Line shutdown, provide fare-free service, and coordinate with the city on traffic mitigation.

items.title: Monkeypox Public Health Strategy
items.summary: Approved a resolution asking the Board of Health to outline its communications and public health approach regarding the monkeypox emergency.

items.title: Zoning Sign Ordinance Review
items.summary: Referred sign regulations in Chapter 94 of the zoning ordinance to the Committee of the Whole for review.

items.title: Demolition Delay Ordinance Revisions
items.summary: Referred a proposed ordinance amendment to the Committee of the Whole that would alter the historical demolition delay review from properties aged 75 years to those built before 1900, while shortening the maximum delay period from 18 months to six months.

items.title: Approval of Tabled Records
items.summary: Approved the minutes of the July 19, 2022 meeting upon Councilor Scarpelli's review.
